To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Shared decision making is a process of patient-clinician interaction that allows patients to make informed health care decisions.
Shared decision making is an important part of patient care.

1) patients who are satisfied with their shared decision making (SDM) process are more likely to have better health outcomes, 2) the quality of SDM is related to the quality of the doctor-patient relationship, and 3) patients’ perceptions of their involvement in decision making is related to their satisfaction with the decision-making process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the process of shared decision making is understood and experienced by patients.
the role of shared decision-making in the management of chronic disease.
the role of patient perceptions of the quality of shared decision making in influencing patient decisional conflict.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patient's perceptions of shared decision-making in healthcare is a very complicated process.
the shared decision making process is an essential part of the medical profession.
patient-centered care and shared decision making are two separate concepts that have been confused with one another.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the patient’s perception of shared decision making is a key component in the process and that this can be measured.
the patient's perceptions of shared decision-making are complex.
we need to understand the patient perspective on shared decision making (SDM) and to develop and test interventions that improve SDM in practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients are interested in and want to engage in shared decision making.
patients' perceptions of shared decision-making are complex and dynamic.
patient perceptions of shared-decision-making (SDM) are not static.
